title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
abstract: Using Google's products and services has always been fundamentally precarious—doing so gives the world's largest advertising company a lot of juicy personal data. Google has long said it won't use the sensitive data from products like Gmail, Drive, and Photos for ad personalization, but a change to the company's privacy policy appears to dismantle that firewall. On October 16, Google issued an update to its privacy policy , spotted by Android Authority . The ad personalization section used to include a clear limit on data from certain apps. "We don’t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos," the document said. Now, Google has updated it with the following language. Updated language on when your sensitive data might inform ads. Credit: Google This equivocation opens the door to using data from apps like Gmail and Photos in ads when it's shared with other Google services, and it just so happens Google has a mechanism for doing that, with Personal Intelligence. The company released Personal Intelligence in early 2026 , allowing users to hand data from multiple apps to Google AI products. The idea is that the added context from your existing data will lead to better AI answers, but it's also proving to be a privacy minefield. Read full article Comments

title: Inside the Pentagon, the pressure is on to find a home for a new spaceport
abstract: Leaders in the US Space Force would like to have a new spaceport up and running in four years, adding a third heavy-lift launch site to relieve pressure from bases in Florida and California that have shot rockets into orbit for nearly 70 years. The obvious problem with that ambition is 2030 is four years away, and Pentagon officials have not determined where the new spaceport should go or how to acquire land for it. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink first mentioned the service's search for a third launch base in May. A congressionally mandated study of the Space Force's launch infrastructure identified the need for "another site that's capable of heavy and super heavy launch capability," Meink said in a House Armed Services Committee hearing. Read full article Comments

title: Spotify ramps up policy enforcement on family plans
abstract: As reported by Music Business Worldwide , Spotify appears to be stepping up enforcement of existing policies regarding Family and Duo subscription plans by requiring users to scan a QR code in person on the plan manager's device in order to maintain access to it. Those who fail to scan the address verification QR code within seven days will see their account demoted to the free tier and be barred from joining any other Duo or Family plan for 12 months. Spotify's QR code plan enforcement. Credit: Spotify Spotify's support documentation verifies the policy after users on Reddit began posting reports of receiving the QR prompt. The enforcement stems from Spotify's requirement that family plan members reside at the same address—a seemingly reasonable policy in concept. But what if you have a child away in college, a spouse who works on the road, or any number of other circumstances that might see families separated by physical distance? The policy could extend beyond friend groups looking to save a buck, affecting actual families who thought they were using the program as intended. Goldman Sachs analysts, in their October 15 Music in the Air: 10 Years On report, made available by HITS Daily Double , estimate that "a meaningful share of family plan users are not actual household members, but rather friends sharing a plan to reduce costs." The report goes on to add, "We see additional monetization upside from tightening household verification on multi-user plans. Most family plans require members to reside at the same address, but enforcement has been minimal in practice." Read full article Comments

title: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
abstract: Much of what we know about how a brain makes decisions comes from studying monkeys watching dots. In a task known as a random-dot-motion task, a cloud of flickering specks drifts weakly in one direction while the subject tries to determine whether—and in which direction— it’s moving. The task has shown that in the primate neocortex, neurons gather visual evidence over time, with their firing rates climbing until they cross a threshold, when the animal commits to a decision. But avian brains don’t have a neocortex, so it wasn’t obvious how they made similar decisions. “This was the big question,” said Andreas Nieder, a neurobiologist at the University of Tübingen. “How [would] a differently organized avian brain encode decisions?” Read full article Comments

title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
abstract: US chip champion Intel was so confused by the US government ban on foreign-made robots that it requested and received a waiver “out of an abundance of caution.” The tech company wanted to make sure that it could continue using certain robotic vehicles in its US chip fabs. The uncertainty surrounding the Federal Communications Commission ban on certain foreign-made robots was revealed in the agency’s decision to grant Intel’s waiver request. On October 22, the FCC published its order allowing Intel to continue using the foreign-made robots in US semiconductor manufacturing facilities for a period of one year. The robots in question are automated guided vehicles operating on “tracks or predefined paths” while often requiring operator oversight, according to Intel’s website. They help to move materials and items around within warehouses and factory floors. Read full article Comments

title: RFK Jr.’s vaccine injury clinic could damage NIH hospital, board warns
abstract: At a recent meeting of the board that oversees the National Institutes of Health's Clinical Center Research Hospital, chair Jack Leslie opened with cheerful introductions and gregarious chatter—then diverted from the agenda of the regularly scheduled meeting. He spent the next six minutes delivering a pointed rebuke of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, warning that his anti-vaccine activities could tarnish the venerable hospital, often called the "house of hope" for patients with rare conditions or those who have exhausted all other options. Leslie took issue with a recent stunt Kennedy had pulled at the hospital, which involved making a surprise appearance for a ribbon-cutting ceremony to open his signature vaccine injury clinic . The ceremony included a panel with people claiming to have been injured by vaccines. They sat behind placards reading "vaccine injured" and spoke with Kennedy and other high-ranking Trump administration officials. Leslie prefaced his comments by noting that some might prefer he not speak out against Kennedy's efforts. "But I think that that would be a failing as an advisory board if we were silent," he said. Leslie also noted that he has no concerns about studying potential injuries from vaccines. "Serious reactions are rare, but real," he said, and people who believe they've been injured should "be taken seriously." Read full article Comments

title: Knicks sent employees fake offer of championship rings in phishing test: Report
abstract: The New York Knicks organization sent employees a phishing email promising free championship rings in a test of its staff's ability to detect scams, The New York Times reported yesterday. “Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here,” the email sent in late September said, instructing employees to click a link to make a selection from two ring designs. Madison Square Garden employees who clicked that link "were forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class to help satisfy some of [owner James] Dolan’s growing cybersecurity concerns," the report said, citing team sources. Dolan is the owner of the Knicks, the New York Rangers, and Madison Square Garden. It's common for corporations to send phishing emails to find out which employees don't pay attention to clues that an email is a scam. A cybersecurity-test email often appears to be from the company itself but includes telltale signs of phishing. For example, Ars Technica owner Condé Nast sends phishing-test messages from email addresses with a misspelled domain, "condenest.com." Read full article Comments

title: Everybody panic: A Valve developer said "HLX" in public
abstract: Gamers still hoping against hope for a true follow-up to Half-Life 2 (after so, so many years ) may remember last year's flurry of speculation that Half-Life 3 was finally nearing completion . Amid all those rumors, though, we never got any official sign from anyone inside Valve that a Half-Life project was currently in development. That changed this week thanks to an apparent slip-up during a panel at GameSoundCon , an industry conference devoted to "the art, technology, and business of game audio." In a panel devoted to Valve's use of open audio engines (captured in this Vimeo clip ), Valve composer and audio artist Mike Morasky let an interesting string of three letters slip while talking about the way the company implements high dynamic range (HDR) audio: Our HDR system is basically that's one of the three pieces that come together to make an HDR that you can easily optimize. And in fact, I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR. HLX has its own version , so on and so forth [emphasis added]. "HLX," of course, has been widely reported as the internal code name for Valve's next Half-Life project. The codename has shown up in Valve engine code since at least 2024 , but it has never been referenced in public by a Valve employee until now (though Morasky was responsible for a close call in an interview last year). Read full article Comments

title: The reactor meant to showcase nuclear’s comeback keeps hitting problems
abstract: US regulators have issued a warning to a nuclear project critical to Donald Trump’s efforts to revive the industry, after a contractor fell into a reactor cavity and a bundle of fuel rods nearly tipped over during refueling. The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission told Holtec International, a company racing to reopen a shuttered reactor at the Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan, to address a “chilled work environment” that has made staff hesitant to raise safety concerns without fear of retaliation. The warning has prompted concerns among critics that financial and political pressures to revitalize nuclear power as an answer to booming AI-driven energy demand are increasing risks of accidents. Read full article Comments

title: Ukraine learns to fight without Starlink as Musk plays politics with satellites
abstract: Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service has played a pivotal role in supporting Ukraine’s successful resistance to Russia’s full-scale invasion for years. But with Starlink having become increasingly unreliable due to Musk’s political inclinations and the latest surprise disruptions to service in Ukraine, the Ukrainians and Europe as a whole are now facing urgent questions about how to move forward without it. As the world’s largest communications satellite network, Starlink can typically support high-speed Internet and data streams for any user or vehicle equipped with a relatively compact Starlink terminal. This has enabled Ukraine to maintain vital communications for both civilian purposes and military operations—and has also expanded the Ukrainian military’s capability to remotely control or provide guidance to drones used in both air defense against Russian attacks and for striking back at Russian targets. “Starlink currently offers some of the best satellite coverage available, with virtually no competitors when you consider the combination of cost, availability, and ease of use,” according to the head of hardware R&D at the Ukrainian defense company BlueBird Tech , who provided comments to Ars anonymously for security reasons. “In practical terms, the main limitation is the need to position the antenna so it can receive signals from the satellites.” Read full article Comments

title: Review: Crystal Lake suffers a bit from its obsession with Pam Voorhees
abstract: Peacock series Crystal Lake doesn’t feel like a Friday the 13th movie when you first press play, even though it’s set up to be a prequel to the original film. (This review includes spoilers of the original Friday the 13th movie but avoids major Crystal Lake spoilers.) Instead, Crystal Lake strives to build a drama that’s half homage, half uncharted territory, while giving a long-awaited backstory to Pamela Voorhees. The original villain in the first film, Pam Voorhees, shocked audiences in 1980 by popping up out of nowhere in the midst of a brutal camp counselor killing spree, then confronting the final girl with a Norman Bates-like delivery of the movie’s chilling tagline, “Kill her, mommy,” using the voice of her drowned son, Jason. Betsy Palmer as Pam Voorhees in Friday the 13th . Credit: via Paramount Pictures Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees in Crystal Lake. Credit: via Peacock Although the hockey-masked killer, Jason Voorhees, became the horror icon at the center of the franchise, his mom, Pam, continued to fascinate fans, who knew very little about her. Beheaded in the first film after just 13 minutes onscreen, her spirit would occasionally appear in later films, but the original actor, Betsy Palmer, who portrayed Pam refused to return, largely because the character has no depth. Read full article Comments

title: Rocket Report: SpaceX says no thanks to military launches; Spanish rocket nearly ready
abstract: Welcome to Edition 9.16 of the Rocket Report! Lots of SpaceX-related news this week including a couple of Thursday shockers. In one story, the company told the US Space Force thanks, but no thanks after being offered three military launch contracts. Then, on the civil space side of things, SpaceX's Starship may required up to 22 refuelings to support a lunar landing, a NASA safety panel said. As always, we welcome reader submissions , and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar. Miura 5 getting closer to launch . PLD Space says its Miura 5 rocket, due to undertake its inaugural launch next year, is nearing final integration, Aviation Week reports . The rocket is one of three Miura 5s the company has already manufactured, with the other two designed to qualify key system elements, CEO Raúl Torres said in an October 19 program update. PLD Space now targets a first flight of the small-lift vehicle before mid-2027. Read full article Comments

title: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
abstract: A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining "userland" access that he says "lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO." The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4 , the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called "tethered" hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access. Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI's Codex to poke at SmileBasic's language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After "substantial effort for ~2 weeks," that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read-and-write access to portions of system memory. Read full article Comments

title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
abstract: Personalized mRNA vaccines against melanoma—the deadliest form of skin cancer—reduced the risk of death or recurrence by 42 percent compared to standard treatment in a late-stage trial, pharmaceutical partners Merck and Moderna announced Thursday . The results are a significant advance in melanoma treatment; Merck and Moderna are already engaging with regulatory authorities to get the vaccine approved. More broadly, the vaccine's success bolsters hope that mRNA vaccines and individualized cancer-targeting medicines offer a new paradigm for cancer therapies. "From the beginning, we believed mRNA technology could make it possible to develop cancer treatments uniquely matched to each patient’s tumor," Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said in a statement. The trial results "mark a defining moment for that vision and show what’s possible when we rethink how medicines are made." They also "reinforce our conviction that mRNA has the potential to fundamentally change how we treat cancer," he said. Read full article Comments

title: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
abstract: NASA does not have, nor want, nuclear weapons. But when it comes to a particular metric that is part of the Artemis Program to land people on the Moon, NASA guards a particular number like it is trying to prevent outsiders from cracking nuclear codes. I am speaking of the number of Starship launches required to fuel a Starship-based lunar lander in low-Earth orbit such that it can fly out to the Moon, land there, and return to lunar orbit. This number has been a moving target over the years. The general response from NASA has typically been, 'We don't know for sure, so we're not going to say.' In 2023, for example, the then-director of NASA's Human Landing System, Lisa Watson-Morgan, told Ars , "We have a general idea, but I’m reluctant to say exactly what that is." Read full article Comments

title: Comcast loses more customers, claims other ISPs' cheap prices are "irrational"
abstract: Comcast reportedly plans significant job cuts in its cable division as the firm continues to lose residential broadband and TV customers. Comcast lost 144,000 residential broadband customers in Q3 2026, up from a 91,000-customer loss in the same quarter a year ago, the company said in its earnings report today. Comcast historically capitalized on a lack of competition for high-speed wired broadband. But now it faces stronger competition from fixed wireless providers and from fiber providers in parts of its cable territory. "Fixed wireless remains aggressive and continues to take share, while fiber construction remains elevated, with pockets of irrational pricing and promotional activity," Comcast co-CEO Mike Cavanagh said today in an earnings call . Read full article Comments

title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
abstract: eMudhra, the certificate authority that issued eight intermediate TLS credentials so weak that anyone could mint certificates for any website or mail server—one had a private encryption key of just 4—said it’s getting out of the business. V. Srinivasan, chairman of India-based eMudhra Limited, cited increasing costs and complexities of compliance requirements—paired with the business generating just 1 percent of its revenue. He also said that the emergence of organizations providing TLS certificates free of charge further reduced returns on investment when compared to other products and services the company offers. Don't let the door hit you on the butt “However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” the company continued in a Thursday post. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.” Read full article Comments

title: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing
abstract: Those mourning yesterday's shuttering of highly praised and influential developer BioWare also had to deal with the cancellation of the next Mass Effect game, which was first teased back in 2020 . Today, we got our best look at what that game could have been with a short, leaked trailer for Mass Effect: Universe . In the roughly two-minute montage—which describes itself as "in-engine footage from our small team" that "uses our pre-production assets"—an ex-military officer wearing an N7 trenchcoat (similar to the one seen in that 2020 teaser) encounters an Asari at a bar. He talks of his frustration with military life—"by the time you put out one fire, another had already started"—before discussing his new line of work "stopping [the fires] before they start" and "making the choices no one else is willing to make. Going where others are afraid to go." Mass Effect: Universe Trailer by u/Random_Hyabusa_Ninja in masseffect Read full article Comments

title: 2026년과 이후 JavaScript의 동향 - 브라우저 밖의 JavaScript
abstract: 브라우저 밖의 JavaScript 동향을 마지막으로 다루었던 2019년 시점( 1부 , 2부 )에서는 Node.js 12와 막 1년을 넘긴 Deno를 소개하며 "Node.js와 같은 성공을 거둘 수 있을지는 아직 미지수"라고 썼습니다. 패키지 관리자 영역은 "npm의 독주 체제"라고 표현했고 npm 회사의 불확실한 상황에 맞서 Entropic, Open-Registry, GitHub Package Registry 같은 도전자가 등장했다고 전했습니다. 7년이 지난 지금 Node.js는 연 1회 릴리스로 일정을 바꾸기로 했습니다. Node.js 호환을 목표로 삼게 된 Deno와 Bun은 각각 Cloudflare와 Anthropic에 합류했고, npm은 GitHub의 일부가 되어 공급망 공격과 싸우고 있습니다. 이번 연재는 다음 네 편으로 구성됩니다. 1편: JavaScript(ECMAScript) 2편: 브라우저 밖의 JavaScript 3편: WebAssembly 4편: 라이브러리와 프레임워크 이 글에서는 먼저 2019년 이후 7년의 변화를 짧게 정리합니다. 이어서 Node.js의 사용 현황과 릴리스 일정, 주요 기능, Deno와 Bun, 서버 런타임 표준인 WinterTC, 공급망 공격으로 크게 바뀐 패키지 관리자와 레지스트리, 데스크톱과 모바일 애플리케이션 개발 도구, PWA와 XR, OpenJS Foundation을 차례로 살펴봅니다. 마지막으로 AI 코딩 도구가 런타임과 패키지 생태계를 어떻게 바꾸었는지 정리합니다. 번들러와 브라우저 밖의 WebAssembly는 짧게 언급만 합니다. WASI와 엣지 플랫폼에서의 WebAssembly 실행은 3편 WebAssembly에서 자세히 다룹니다. 이 글의 내용은 2026년 10월을 기준으로 작성되었습니다. 글을 읽는 시점에 따라 글의 내용과 사실이 다를 수 있습니다. 2019년 이후 7년 2019년 글을 쓸 때 Node.js의 최신 버전은 12.13이었습니다. 2026년 10월 현재 최신 버전은 26.12이고 그사이 메이저 버전이 열네 번 나왔습니다(참고: Node.js 26.12.0 릴리스 ). 숫자보다 큰 변화는 런타임의 역할입니다. 2019년의 Node.js는 서버와 빌드 도구를 실행하는 런타임이었다면, 지금의 Node.js는 TypeScript 파일을 바로 실행하고 테스트 러너와 SQLite, WebSocket 클라이언트를 내장하며 권한 모델로 파일과 네트워크 접근을 제한합니다. 2019년에 별도 패키지를 설치해야 했던 기능 상당수가 런타임에 내장되었습니다. 경쟁 구도도 달라졌습니다. 2019년에는 Node.js와 Deno를 비교했지만 지금은 Bun까지 세 런타임이 Node.js 호환성을 두고 경쟁합니다. 다만 2026년 10월 Deno 팀이 Cloudflare에 합류하면서 Deno 런타임의 개발은 1년 뒤 끝나게 되었습니다. 패키지 생태계에서는 2020년 GitHub이 npm을 인수하면서 2019년 글이 걱정한 "기술 외적인 불확실성"이 해소되었습니다. 그 대신 2025년부터는 공급망 공격이 가장 큰 문제가 되었습니다. 메인테이너 계정을 탈취해 악성 버전을 올리는 공격이 반복되었고 스스로 퍼지는 웜까지 등장했습니다. npm과 pnpm은 설치 스크립트를 기본으로 실행하지 않도록 바꾸었습니다. 표 1 2019년 이후 브라우저 밖의 JavaScript 주요 사건 시기 사건 2020년 3월 GitHub, npm 인수 발표 (4월 인수 완료) 2021년 9월 Electron, 8주 릴리스 주기로 전환 (Electron 15) 2024년 10월 Deno 2 출시 , Tauri 2.0 출시 , React Native 0.76에서 새 아키텍처 기본화 2024년 12월 Node.js 22.12에서 require(esm) 플래그 제거 2025년 1월 WinterCG가 Ecma TC55(WinterTC)로 이동, pnpm 10에서 의존성 설치 스크립트 기본 미실행 2025년 9월 chalk, debug 등 메인테이너 계정 탈취 , Shai-Hulud 웜 2025년 11월 npm classic 토큰 생성 중단 , Shai-Hulud 2.0 2025년 12월 npm classic 토큰 전체 폐기 , Anthropic의 Bun 인수 , ECMA-429 1판 승인 2026년 3월 Node.js 릴리스 일정 개편 발표 , Axios 계정 탈취 2026년 7월 npm 12, 설치 스크립트 기본 미실행 2026년 8월 Bun 1.4 (Rust 재작성), pnpm 12 (Rust 재작성), vlt 1.0 2026년 10월 Deno 팀, Cloudflare 합류 , Deno 런타임 개발 사실상 종료(1년간 보안 업데이트 후 종료), Deno Deploy 6개월 뒤 종료 Node.js 2019년 글은 마무리에서 "Node.js는 주요 개발 선택 사항 중 하나로 당당하게 인정받고 있다"고 평가했습니다. 7년 뒤의 지표를 보면 이 평가는 더 굳어졌습니다. 그사이 Node.js는 ESM과 TypeScript 지원에서 큰 진전을 이뤘고 릴리스 방식도 바꾸었습니다. 지표로 보는 Node.js Stack Overflow 2025 개발자 설문에서 Node.js는 '웹 프레임워크와 기술' 항목 1위를 차지했습니다. 전체 응답자의 48.7%, 전문 개발자의 49.1%가 Node.js를 사용한다고 답했습니다. 같은 항목에서 Deno는 4%였고, Bun은 '클라우드 개발' 항목에서 5.5%였습니다(참고: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025: Technology ). State of JS 2025의 JavaScript 런타임 문항(응답자 11,141명)에서도 순서는 같습니다(표 2). 조사 측은 "Bun의 3위는 프로젝트 성장의 좋은 신호"라고 평했습니다(참고: State of JS 2025: Other Tools ). 표 2 State of JS 2025 JavaScript 런타임 사용 응답 수(출처: State of JS 2025 ) 런타임 응답 수 Node.js 10,062 브라우저 9,682 Bun 2,321 Service Workers 1,660 Cloudflare Workers 1,294 Deno 1,244 이 설문에서 Node.js의 사용 응답 수는 Bun과 Deno 각각의 네 배 이상입니다. 다만 Bun과 Deno가 Node.js 호환을 목표로 삼으면서 Node.js 코드를 실행할 수 있는 런타임이 Node.js만은 아니게 되었습니다. 릴리스 관리와 새 연간 일정 2019년 글에서 설명한 연 2회 메이저 릴리스 (짝수 버전은 장기 지원(LTS), 홀수 버전은 단기 지원)는 2026년까지 유지되었습니다. Node.js는 2026년 3월 릴리스 일정 개편을 발표했습니다(참고: Evolving the Node.js Release Schedule ). 약 10년간 이어 온 연 2회 메이저 릴리스를 Node.js 27부터 연 1회로 바꿉니다. 매년 4월 메이저 버전을 출시하고 10월에 LTS로 전환합니다. 홀짝 구분 없이 모든 버전이 LTS가 됩니다. 메이저 출시 전 6개월 동안 하위 호환을 깨는 변경(semver-major)을 허용하는 알파 채널( 27.0.0-alpha.1 형식)을 운영합니다. 버전 번호를 출시 연도에 맞춥니다. 27.0.0은 2027년, 28.0.0은 2028년에 나옵니다. 그림 1 Node.js 24부터 30까지의 릴리스 일정(27부터 새 일정 적용, 출처: Evolving the Node.js Release Schedule ) 발표문은 개편 이유로 홀수 버전의 채택률이 매우 낮았다는 데이터와, 대부분 자원봉사자인 메인테이너가 네다섯 개의 릴리스 라인에 보안 패치를 동시에 내보내는 부담을 들었습니다. 표 3 Node.js 릴리스 현황(2026년 10월, 출처: nodejs/Release ) 버전 상태 주요 내용 22(Jod) Maintenance LTS, 2027년 4월 종료 require(esm) 플래그 제거 24(Krypton) Active LTS, 10월 20일 Maintenance 전환 V8 13.6, using , Error.isError , RegExp.es

title: 카카오 AI 돛 Summit 26 다시보기 공개 — AI 인프라부터 서비스 적용, 개발과 창업까지
abstract: 지난 9월 29일 부산에서 약 800명의 참가자와 함께한 ‘카카오 AI 돛 Summit 26’의 주요 세션 VOD를 공개합니다. 👉 카카오 AI 돛 Summit 26 세션 VOD 보러 가기 AI와 함께 개발하는 방식부터 실제 서비스에 AI를 적용하는 과정, 연구를 창업으로 연결하는 경험까지. 현장에 참석하지 못했거나 동시에 진행되어 놓쳤던 발표를 이제 온라인에서 만나보세요. 어떤 세션부터 볼지 고민된다면, 지금 여러분의 관심사와 가장 가까운 이야기부터...

title: 머릿속에 있던 로그 정의 기준을 모두의 AI 스킬로 만들기
abstract: 토스 앱에서 사용자가 어떤 화면을 보고 무엇을 눌렀는지는 앱로그로 남아요. 토스는 이렇게 쌓이는 로그를 서비스 품질을 높이는 목적으로 사용해요. 그래서 로그를 처음부터 정확하고 일관되게 정의해야 분석 결과도 믿을 수 있어요. 이를 위해 로그를 전담해 설계하고 관리하는 DataOps Manager와 로그 명세를 한곳에서 관리하는 플랫폼인 로그센터가 있어요. DataOps Manager는 앱로그의 규칙과 맥락을 지키며 담당 도메인의 로그 명세를 정의하고 관리 해요. 이번 글에서는 비개발자인 DataOps Manager들이 모여 로그센터에서 수동으로 진행하던 로그 정의 업무를 AI 스킬로 개선한 과정 을 소개하려고 해요. 1. 로그 정의할 때 중요한 것들 앱 화면은 끊임없이 새로 생기고 바뀌어요. 그때마다 DataOps Manager(DOM)는 사용자의 행동을 어떤 로그로 기록할지, 그 로그에 어떤 파라미터를 함께 남길지 새로 정해야 해요. 로그를 정의할 때에는 다음 네 가지를 챙겨야 해요. 로그를 정의할 때에는 로그를 정해진 형식에 따라서, 도메인 안의 맥락을 이어서, 분석에 필요한 것만 남기면서, 정책과 안전을 지켜서 정의해야 해요. 로그 규칙은 '앱로그 백과사전'에 정리되어 있었어요. 하지만 로그를 정의할 때는 규칙뿐 아니라 도메인의 맥락과 히스토리도 중요해요. 기존 로그 명세를 직접 검색해 참고할 수는 있었지만, 도메인의 맥락은 담당 DOM의 머릿속에 남아 있는 경우가 많았어요. 그래서 각자가 가진 맥락과 경험에 의존해 로그센터에서 수동으로 로그를 정의하고 관리했어요. 한 사람이 정확하게 정의하기도, 모두가 일관되게 정의하기도 어려웠던 부분을 저희는 AI 스킬로 로그를 정의하는 방식과 과정 모두를 개선 하고자 했어요. 2. 로그 정의 과정을 AI 스킬로 옮기기 로그를 정의할 때마다 앞에서 본 네 가지 규칙을 찾아보고 도메인의 맥락까지 기억하는 건 쉽지 않은 일이었어요. 그래서 한 DOM이 자신이 알고 있던 규칙과 경험을 살려, 로그 정의를 돕는 작은 스킬을 만들어 쓰기 시작했어요. 하지만 이 스킬은 만든 사람의 도메인과 경험에 묶여 있어서, 만든 사람은 편했지만 다른 사람이나 다른 도메인에서는 그대로 쓰기 어려웠어요. 그래서 저희는 이 스킬을 누가 어떤 도메인에서 작업하든 함께 쓸 수 있도록 제대로 풀어보기로 했어요. 로그를 정의할 때 거치는 판단과 순서를 개인의 머릿속이 아니라 스킬 안에 담으면, 매번 규칙을 외우지 않아도 되고 모든 도메인에서 같은 기준으로 정의할 수 있으니까요. 그렇게 만든 '로그 정의 스킬'은 로그 명세를 대신 찍어내는 생성기는 아니에요. 새 로그를 만들기 전에 '앱로그 백과사전'의 표준을 확인하고 도메인의 기존 로그 명세를 끝까지 조회해 재사용할 수 있는지 먼저 살피고 , 실제 반영은 사람이 확정한 뒤에만 실행해요. (이 스킬은 사용자의 로그를 읽거나 처리하지 않아요.) 화면 하나의 로그를 정의해달라고 하면 로그 정의 스킬은 다음의 순서로 움직여요. 스킬은 화면 디자인을 살펴보고, 적절한 로그 명세 규칙을 확인한 뒤 재사용할 수 있는 부분을 검토해 로그 명세를 제안해요. DOM이 제안된 명세를 검토해 최종 확정하면, 스킬이 이를 시스템에 반영해요. 이 과정에서 스킬, 로그센터의 CLI(Command Line Interface)인 lctl , 로그센터는 역할을 나눠 맡아요. 스킬은 맥락에 따른 판단을 안내하고, 확신할 수 없는 부분은 사람에게 물어요. 로그 이름 형식처럼 기계가 판정할 수 있는 규칙은 lctl 이 저장 전에 검사하고, 로그센터는 규칙에 맞지 않는 명세의 발행을 거절해요. 형식 규칙은 스킬에 적어두지 않고 실행할 때마다 lctl 에 묻기 때문에, 규칙이 바뀌어도 스킬은 늘 최신 기준을 따를 수 있어요. 로그 정의 스킬이 판단하고 조율하면, 로그센터 CLI가 저장 전에 미리 걸러내고, 로그센터가 저장하며 최종 판정해요. 3. 개인 도구에서 팀 표준으로 로그 정의 스킬을 함께 쓰려니 개인이 사용할 때보다 고려해야 할 게 많았어요. 한 사람의 업무에 맞춰져 있던 안내를 여러 DOM이 활용할 수 있도록 다듬고, 이후에 보완한 내용도 함께 관리할 방법이 필요했죠. 마침 로그센터와 lctl 을 개발 및 관리하는 로그 프로덕트팀에서 스킬을 lctl 에 포함해 함께 배포하자는 제안을 해주셨어요. 협업 과정에서는 문서 구조도 개선했어요. 처음엔 한 문서에 규칙과 절차를 다 담았는데, 길어질수록 AI가 중요한 규칙을 놓쳤거든요. 로그 프로덕트팀의 프론트엔드(FE, Frontend) 개발자분께 기술 검토를 받아, 한 문서에 모여 있던 규칙과 절차를 작업별로 나누고, 스킬에는 각 문서를 찾아가는 안내를 남겼어요. AI가 매번 긴 문서를 읽지 않고, 해당 작업에 필요한 내용만 찾아 읽을 수 있게 된 거예요. 이번 기회로 일하는 방식도 달라졌어요. 기존에는 업무 도구를 개선할 때, 실사용자로서 필요한 기능과 업무 맥락을 기획 과정에 전달했어요. 하지만 이번에는 그 맥락을 가장 잘 아는 저희가 AI를 활용해 필요한 도구를 직접 만들었어요. 그리고 플랫폼 조직인 로그 프로덕트팀은 저희가 만든 스킬을 검토한 후 lctl 에 통합해 배포하는 일을 맡아주셨어요. 기존에는 현업에서 문제를 발견하면 로그 프로덕트팀에 수정을 요청하고, 작업이 끝날 때까지 기다린 뒤 해결 여부를 확인했어요. 지금은 현업에서 발굴한 개선점을 DOM이 AI 스킬로 직접 개발하고, 로그 프로덕트팀과 협업해 로그센터 CLI에 통합 배포했어요. 업무를 아는 사람이 직접 만든 해결 방법에 플랫폼 조직의 기술과 운영 경험이 더해지면서, 동료들도 함께 쓰는 도구로 발전시킬 수 있었어요. 4. 더 수월하게, 더 일관되게 로그 정의하기 스킬을 함께 쓰기 시작하면서, DOM이 로그를 정의하는 과정과 시간을 쓰는 곳도 달라졌어요. 예전에는 디자인이 나오면 DOM이 화면을 보며 필요한 로그를 설계했어요. 기존 로그 명세를 재사용할 수 있는지 찾아보고, 새로 만들어야 한다면 이름과 구조를 정했죠. 스크린샷을 준비하고, 정리한 명세를 로그센터에 하나씩 입력하는 일도 직접 했어요. 지금은 디자인과 필요한 맥락을 전달하면 스킬이 기존 로그 명세와 파라미터를 조회하고, 재사용 후보와 새로운 명세를 제안해요. DOM이 검토해 확정하면 lctl 로 로그센터에 반영하죠. 기존에는 DOM이 디자인 확인부터 명세 수기 입력까지 각 단계를 하나씩 직접 처리했어요. 지금은 DOM이 화면과 맥락을 전달하면 스킬이 기존 정의를 조회해 명세 초안을 쓰고, DOM은 분석 목적과 전체 구조를 검토해 명세를 확정해요. 로그의 목적과 전체 구조에 더 집중해요. 로그를 하나씩 찾아 작성하고 옮겨 적는 일이 줄면서, 사용자 흐름 전체를 살피는 데 더 시간을 쓸 수 있게 됐어요. 스킬이 제안한 명세와 추가 정보를 바탕으로, 서비스 품질을 높이는 데 필요한 정보가 빠짐없이 정의됐는지 검토해요. 기존 로그와의 연결성을 지키기 쉬워졌어요. 예전에는 기존 정의를 직접 찾아 대조하다 보니, 이미 card_company 로 남기던 정보를 놓치고 issuer 처럼 다른 이름으로 정의할 위험이 있었어요. 지금은 스킬이 기존 로그 명세와 파라미터를 먼저 조회해 재사용 후보를 제안해요. 담당자가 의미와 사용 맥락을 확인한 뒤 재사용하면서, 같은 정보를 일관된 이름과 구조로 남기고 기존 로그와 연결해 분석하기 쉬워졌어요. 각자 챙기던 규칙과 절차를 함께 관리해요. 예전에는 로그 이름과 이벤트 타입의 규칙, 명세를 반영하는 절차를 각자 찾아보고 적용했어요. 이제는 같은 스킬을 사용해 담당자가 달라도 공통된 기준과 순서에 따라 작업할 수 있어요. 사용하면서 보완한 내용도 스킬에 반영하면 다음 작업부터 동료들이 함께 활용할 수 있고요. 로그 정의 스킬을 직접 사용한 동료들은 이렇게 이야기해주셨어요. “화면에서 새로 정의할 퍼널을 짚어 주기만 했는데 로그가 알맞게 정의돼서 정말 편했어요! 신규 파라미터나 ENUM을 지정하려면 원래 여러 단계를 차례로 거쳐야 하는데, 이제는 요청을 입력하기만 하면 바로 처리되어서 로그 정의 과정이 아주 쾌적해졌어요!” “제가 생각한 가치는 로그를 대신 만들어주는 것보다, 로그 스키마 생성 정책을

title: 모델만 바꿨는데 LLM 비용이 3배가 된 이유
abstract: 안녕하세요, 당근 커뮤니티홈팀에서 백엔드를 개발하는 제이(Jay)예요. 당근 앱의 커뮤니티 탭에는 이웃이 알려 주는 동네 정보부터 소소한 일상과 취미까지 나누는 동네생활, 모임, 카페, 아파트가 모여 있어요. 커뮤니티홈팀은 이 서비스들의 글을 한데 모아 보여 주는 피드를 맡고 있어요. 피드를 맡으며 가장 고민하는 건 사용자에게 더 알맞은 글을 어떻게 보여 줄지예요. 그래서 기존 머신러닝 추천에 더해, LLM으로 글의 다양한 메타데이터를 뽑아 추천에 쓰고 있어요. 그중 하나가 LLM에 카테고리 목록과 글을 주고 어느 주제에 속하는지 고르게 하는 주제 분류예요. 추천은 보여 줄 글 후보를 모으는 단계와 그 순서를 정하는 단계로 나뉘는데, 글마다 주제가 붙어 있으면 첫 단계부터 사용자가 관심 있는 주제의 글을 골라 올 수 있어요. 주제 분류를 할 때 LLM에 보내는 요청을 열어 보면 대부분이 매번 똑같은 지시문과 카테고리 목록이고, 글 본문은 끝에 조금 붙어 있을 뿐이에요. 이 글에서는 요청마다 똑같은 이 부분을 고정부라고 부를게요. 2026년 8월, 이 작업의 모델을 Gemini에서 단가가 20% 낮은 OpenAI GPT-5.6으로 바꿨어요. 응답은 정상이었고 에러도 한 건 없었어요. 닷새 뒤 보니 단가는 내렸는데 요청당 비용은 3.2배가 돼 있었어요. 원인은 프롬프트 캐시였어요. 입력 중 캐시에서 읽어 온 비율인 캐시 히트율이 85.8%에서 2.3%로 떨어져 있었죠. 교체 전후의 응답을 나란히 놓으면 달라진 곳은 사용량 정보 안의 캐시 필드 하나뿐이었어요. 캐시가 깨져도 에러는 나지 않아요. 비용만 늘어요. 이 글은 그 일을 해결하며 알게 된 것을 정리한 기록이에요. 캐시가 무엇을 재사용하는지, 비용은 어떻게 매겨지는지, 언제 켜지고 어디까지 저장되는지, 캐시에서 읽었는지는 어떻게 확인하는지를 OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini를 나란히 놓고 살펴봐요. 같은 지시문에 입력만 바꿔 LLM을 대량으로 부르거나, 챗봇이나 에이전트처럼 앞부분이 같은 요청을 되풀이해 보내는 분이라면 참고가 될 거예요. 프롬프트 캐시의 원리 신입 검수자에게 매번 규정집 20쪽과 오늘 볼 글 한 편을 함께 준다고 해 볼게요. 규정집은 늘 같고 글만 바뀌는데, 이 검수자는 기억을 못 해서 글마다 규정집을 처음부터 다시 읽어요. 하루 10만 편이면 규정집을 10만 번 읽는 셈이에요. LLM도 똑같이 요청마다 프롬프트 전체를 처음부터 다시 읽어요. 이 낭비를 줄이는 게 프롬프트 캐시예요. 앞 토큰을 돌아보는 어텐션 LLM은 글을 토큰 단위로 하나씩 이어 써요. 다음 토큰을 고르기 전에는 앞 토큰들을 돌아보며 무엇을 참고할지 따지는데, 이 계산을 어텐션(attention)이라고 해요. “어제 시장에서 산 사과를 깎아서” 다음에 올 토큰을 고른다고 해 볼게요. 사람은 바로 “먹었다”를 떠올려요. “사과”와 “깎아서”가 가장 관련 있고 “어제”나 “시장에서”는 덜 중요하다는 걸 알기 때문이에요. 모델은 이 판단을 마지막 토큰 “깎아서” 자리에서 숫자로 해요. 어텐션에는 토큰마다 세 가지 값이 쓰여요. 도서관에서 자료를 찾는 일에 비유해 볼게요. Q(Query, 질문) : 마지막 토큰이 다음 토큰을 고르려고 들고 있는 질문이에요. “무엇을 했는지 이어 쓰려면 어떤 정보가 필요하지?” 같은 것이에요. K(Key, 분류표) : 앞 토큰마다 붙은 꼬리표예요. 책의 분류표처럼 “먹을 수 있는 물건”, “때를 나타내는 말” 같은 정보를 담아요. V(Value, 내용) : 앞 토큰이 실제로 건네주는 정보예요. 책의 본문에 해당해요. 마지막 토큰 “깎아서”는 자기 Q를 앞 토큰들(자기 자신 포함)의 K와 하나씩 맞춰 보고 점수를 매겨요. “사과”와 “깎아서”는 높은 점수를, “어제”는 낮은 점수를 받아요. 그다음 점수 비율대로 V를 섞고 그 결과로 다음 토큰 “먹었다”를 골라요. 분류표(K)로 관련 있는 책을 고른 뒤, 그 책들의 본문(V)을 점수만큼 읽는 것과 같아요. 실제 Q, K, V는 사람이 읽을 수 있는 문장이 아니라 숫자 묶음(벡터)이고, 위 설명은 그 역할을 말로 푼 거예요. 한 번 만들면 계속 쓰는 K와 V “먹었다”를 고른 뒤에는 “먹었다”가 Q를 들고 같은 일을 해요. 이때 “어제”부터 “깎아서”까지의 K와 V는 앞 단계에서 만든 것과 똑같아요. 뒤에 어떤 토큰이 붙어도 앞 토큰의 K와 V는 바뀌지 않거든요. 그래서 모델은 한 번 만든 K와 V를 캐시에 쌓아 두고 다시 꺼내 써요. 이 캐시를 KV 캐시라고 해요. 새로 계산하는 건 새 토큰의 Q, K, V뿐이고, Q는 그 토큰이 앞을 볼 때 한 번 쓰고 끝나서 쌓아 두지 않아요. 캐시가 없다면 토큰을 하나 쓸 때마다 앞 토큰 전부를 처음부터 다시 계산해야 해요. 입력도 마찬가지예요. 모델은 답을 쓰기 전에 입력 전체를 한꺼번에 읽으며 K와 V를 만들어 캐시를 채워요. 이 단계를 prefill이라고 하는데, 입력이 길수록 오래 걸려요. KV 캐시를 다음 요청에 물려주는 프롬프트 캐시 KV 캐시는 원래 요청 하나가 끝나면 함께 사라져요. 프롬프트 캐시는 그 앞부분을 요청이 끝난 뒤에도 서버에 남겨 두는 기능이에요. 다음 요청의 앞부분이 같으면 prefill을 건너뛰고 남겨 둔 것을 그대로 꺼내 써요. 캐시에서 읽은 앞부분은 Q, K, V 어느 것도 다시 계산하지 않고 새로 들어온 토큰만 계산해요. 규정집을 읽으며 만든 메모를 다음 글에도 쓰는 셈이에요. 제공사는 아낀 계산만큼 값을 깎아 주는데, OpenAI는 캐시에서 읽은 입력 토큰을 최대 95%까지 할인해요. 헷갈리기 쉬운 것 프롬프트 캐시는 응답 캐시가 아니에요. 응답 캐시는 같은 질문에 저장해 둔 답을 그대로 돌려줘요. 뜻이 비슷한 질문에도 답을 돌려주는 시맨틱 캐싱도 응답 캐시의 한 종류예요. 프롬프트 캐시는 입력을 읽는 계산만 재사용하고 출력은 매번 새로 만들어요. 캐시를 켜도 답의 품질은 그대로예요. 답을 만드는 과정은 캐시가 없을 때와 똑같다고 OpenAI와 Anthropic 문서 모두 적어 두었어요. 캐시는 입력 비용만 깎아요. 출력 토큰은 캐시와 상관없이 정가예요. 응답도 빨리 시작돼요. 입력을 처리하는 시간이 줄어서예요. 다만 공식 문서에 일반적인 수치는 없어요. 앞부분이 글자 하나까지 같아야 하는 이유 모델 구조 때문이에요. 모델은 여러 층으로 되어 있고, 층마다 가중치가 달라서 같은 어텐션이라도 층마다 다른 질문을 던져요. 아래층의 결과는 위층의 입력이 돼요. 예를 들어 아래층에서 “깎아서”가 “사과를”과 묶이면, 위층의 “깎아서”는 이미 “사과를 깎아서”라는 뜻을 담고 다시 앞을 봐요. 이렇게 층을 지날수록 앞 문맥이 쌓이니, 위층의 K와 V는 그 토큰 하나가 아니라 앞 토큰 전체에 묶여 있어요. 앞에서 토큰 하나만 달라져도 그 뒤의 K와 V는 모두 달라져요. 위치도 따져요. K에는 “몇 번째 토큰인가”라는 정보가 섞여 있어서 같은 문장도 100번째와 200번째에서 K가 달라요. 그래서 프롬프트 캐시가 다시 쓸 수 있는 건 처음부터 똑같은 부분뿐이에요. 중간에 한 번이라도 다른 토큰이 나오면, 그 뒤가 아무리 똑같아도 다시 계산해요. 예를 들어 프롬프트 맨 앞의 시각 2026-09-04 09:00이 1분 뒤 09:01로 바뀌면, 토큰 하나 차이인데도 그 뒤 지시문 전체를 다시 계산해요. 시각을 맨 뒤로 옮기면 끝의 몇 토큰만 새로 계산해요. 앞부분을 흔드는 것들 OpenAI 문서에 따르면 캐시되는 앞부분에는 OpenAI가 자체로 넣는 지시문, 개발자 메시지, 도구 정의, 대화 이력까지 들어가요. 그래서 프롬프트 문구를 고치지 않아도, 요청마다 끼어드는 값이나 함께 보내는 설정이 바뀌면 앞부분이 달라져요. 앞쪽에 넣은 시각과 날짜. Research communities thrive through collaboration, the exchange of ideas, and opportunities to connect across institutions […]

title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
abstract: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.

title: Evaluating the Applicability of LLM Inference Optimizations on Apple Silicon
abstract: Apple Silicon is among the most widely used platforms for local LLM inference, yet nearly all inference optimizations are designed and validated on server-class NVIDIA GPUs under batched serving workloads. Which optimizations retain their benefits when moved to Apple Silicon, and what determines their applicability? We evaluate four optimization families: KV-cache pruning, speculative decoding, ported GPU kernels, and post-training quantization. Experiments span four Apple machines under a common single-request decode workload, with matched RTX 4090 comparisons where possible. KV-cache pruning can reach up to 1.75 times end-to-end throughput on Apple but can reduce throughput on desktop NVIDIA GPUs. Under the common benchmark, all evaluated speculative decoding methods reduce throughput on Apple, despite reported 2-6 times gains on server GPUs. CUDA kernel designs transfer only partially: public Metal lacks asynchronous copy, and batch-one decode makes several serving-oriented mechanisms inapplicable, although transferable components yield up to 1.20 times decode throughput. Quantization gains vary by machine. Across four families, a reported speedup is not a portable property of a technique alone but a joint function of technique, runtime, hardware contract, and workload regime.

title: PointerBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained GUI Grounding
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models have shown promising performance in computer-use tasks, from planning user workflows to grounding natural-language actions to precise UI targets. Existing end-to-end benchmarks primarily emphasize long-horizon task completion, while GUI grounding benchmarks remain focused on conventional controls and a limited set of professional interfaces. We introduce POINTERBENCH, a diagnostic suite of 1,500 screenshot-instruction pairs probing three complementary capabilities: thin sub-element identification and geometric grounding in spreadsheets (POINTERBENCH-Sheets), character-level grounding in long-text documents (POINTERBENCH-Text), and mixed GUI grounding across 100 professional applications (POINTERBENCH-Pro). We carefully curate each task with pixel-exact target geometry and evaluate both general-purpose multimodal models and 39 specialist GUI grounding configurations. We find text grounding to be the most challenging setting, with Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the leading native specialist UI-Venus-2-9B achieving 69.6%, 53.4%, and 25.8% success on POINTERBENCH-Text despite respective 83.2%, 77.7%, and 54.5% average success across POINTERBENCH. These results reveal substantial headroom in fine-grained GUI grounding across frontier and specialist models. We publicly release the benchmark and evaluation code at https://github.com/warmwindOS/pointerbench.

title: On the Calibration of Isotonic Distributional Regression
abstract: Isotonic distributional regression (IDR) has recently been proposed as a non-parametric technique for probabilistic forecasting via the estimation of conditional distributions under order restrictions, based on continuous outcomes from deterministic model outputs. IDR has been widely used and multiple studies report promising performance and well-calibrated forecasts across application domains. We document a peculiar out-of-sample artifact of IDR, where probability integral transform (PIT) values are rational fractions with empirical frequencies resembling Thomae's function, an effect which thus far seems to have been overlooked. This phenomenon is demonstrated empirically using meteorological data and a simulation study. We further provide a theoretical explanation linking the spiking behavior to the discrete structure of the isotonic fits, and discuss how this artifact can be mitigated via smoothing approaches.

title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering
abstract: Long-context models often use answer-bearing evidence less effectively when it appears away from a prompt boundary. We compare this position bias across Transformer, state-space, and hybrid Mamba architectures by moving one gold document through a fixed set of nine distractors. The evaluated Transformers show a beginning advantage that the evaluated state-space models lack, while both families favor evidence near the end. A matched pure-versus-hybrid Mamba comparison points in the same direction but remains statistically uncertain. The family difference appears among models that can answer the task. Transformer primacy reappears on synthetic retrieval, where state-space ceiling prevents a family comparison. A corpus swap within one state-space architecture changes overall accuracy without a detectable change in curve shape. Prompt changes can create or nearly remove a beginning advantage. Position remains decodable across architectures even when response curves differ, and attention concentration near initial tokens covaries with beginning sensitivity in the tested Transformer family. These exploratory results show that effective context use depends on the evaluated architecture family, capability, task, and prompt, without isolating the sequence mixer as the sole cause.

title: Post-Audit Mirage: Identifiability Limits of Offline Agent Verification
abstract: Offline tests can fail to reveal whether an agent update will remain safe after deployment. We operationalize this post-audit mirage using matched safe and harmful lifecycles that expose identical verifier-visible evidence while an isolated scorer records opposite deployment truth. Our theorem applies standard observational-equivalence and indistinguishability ideas to this executable audit boundary and states the resulting error-abstention tradeoff. The Post-Audit Mirage benchmark makes that boundary executable across authorization, scheduling, and shared-capacity environments. IdentifiedRangeMonitor uses fresh group-labelled harm outcomes to return deploy, hold, cannot determine, or unsupported. Experiments show that monitoring can recover the missing distinction in favorable settings but may remain undecided for rare groups, small effects, or missing observations. Verifier-agent evaluation must therefore test both calculation validity and whether the available evidence supports the deployment decision.

title: What Comes Next and Why: Interpretable Next-Event Prediction with Neuro-Symbolic Rules
abstract: In real-world applications, being able to explain why a prediction is made is often as important - if not more so - than achieving high accuracy. However, existing methods for sequential event prediction typically prioritize accuracy at the expense of interpretability. Neuro-symbolic approaches offer a promising direction to improve interpretability by learning symbolic rules, but extending them to next-event prediction is challenging due to the presence of temporal dependencies. We introduce RULES, a neuro-symbolic model that learns sequential rules directly from data, and combine it with a residual network to form RUNES (Rule Network for Event Sequences). RULES accurately recovers ground truth rules from synthetic data and discovers compact, interpretable rule sets on real data. RUNES combines these rules additively with a residual network, achieving competitive accuracy while providing transparent access to active rules and how residuals adjust predictions.

title: Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters for Utility-Preserving Anti-Distillation
abstract: While reasoning traces improve model capability, they also provide supervision signals for downstream distillation. Initial efforts to mitigate this issue rely on decoding-time interventions, but they incur high inference overhead and can harm the teacher model's natural fluency. We propose Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters (CALA), a lightweight training-time defense. CALA attaches a small residual adapter to a frozen teacher model and trains only the adapter. A proxy student identifies positions where imitation is most sensitive, and the adapter perturbs the output distribution at these positions while remaining within high-probability regions. A conflict-aware optimization strategy balances anti-distillation and utility objectives, while regularization preserves the teacher's performance and fluency. At inference time, CALA incurs modest overhead and requires no auxiliary model. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that CALA substantially reduces successful student imitation while maintaining near-original teacher performance and generation quality. These results establish CALA as a practical and efficient alternative to decoding-time approaches.

title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model
abstract: Soil moisture and temperature govern plant-water availability and microbial activity, making them key indicators for evaluating land-restoration efforts on degraded landscapes. However, the physical and data-driven models normally used to forecast them both need information that a newly instrumented restoration site does not yet have: hydraulic parameters for the former and months of per-site training data for the latter. We evaluate TimesFM 1, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on 15-minute telemetry from 27 sensor stations across three land-management regimes (Control, Treatment, Scald) at a semi-arid restoration site, forecasting 5 cm and 30 cm soil moisture and enclosure temperature at seven lead times from 1 h to 168 h. Using gap-aware rolling-origin evaluation across sensors, we find that TimesFM beats the best rule-based statistical forecasting baselines (persistence, seasonal-naive, or 7-day climatology) by 21-76% at sub-daily lead times but loses by 6-79% beyond a day, a pattern explained by a diurnal-alignment mechanism that holds for both soil-moisture depths and temperature. A CatBoost baseline trained walk-forward on the same origins with full history and weather covariates never wins overall, and we show that its weakness is partly a cold-start effect specific to short deployments. We additionally quantify the inference cost of zero-shot forecasting on commodity CPU hardware. Our results highlight a practical trade-off between zero-shot forecasting capability, predictive performance, and computational efficiency.

title: Random Initialization as a Baseline for Time Series Foundation Models
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) use self-supervised pretraining to learn reusable representations for downstream tasks such as multivariate time series classification (MTSC). We examine how much pretrained weights contribute beyond the architecture itself by comparing seven publicly released instances from four TSFM families with architecture-matched randomly initialized counterparts on the UEA MTSC archive. For each instance, five random initializations are evaluated using four classifiers on frozen representations: ridge classification, logistic regression, RBF SVM, and random forest. After model-specific exclusions due to computational constraints, the study comprises 183 paired dataset-level comparisons. Pretraining improves mean accuracy for all seven instances, but the gains are modest, ranging from 1.43 to 5.19 percentage points, with an overall average improvement of 2.58 points. Three of seven per-instance Wilcoxon signed-rank tests have raw $p$-values below 0.05, but only NuTime remains significant after Holm correction. A secondary pooled test across all 183 pairs gives $p < 0.001$, while the corrected per-instance tests remain the primary evidence. We also compare with ROCKET, Hydra, and Quant, which remain competitive without requiring large-scale pretraining. These findings suggest that MTSC evaluations should distinguish the effect of pretrained weights from that of the underlying architecture and should include both architecture-matched random initialization and strong non-pretrained baselines.

title: Bifurcations from Weight Space: JEPAWG on Parametric Dynamical Systems
abstract: Trained network weights are increasingly treated as data, but there is rarely ground truth about what a population of models should encode, which hampers systematic validation of weight-space methods. This makes parametric dynamical systems a natural test-bed: the dynamics change qualitatively at submanifolds of parameter space that are, in well-studied families, known analytically or numerically. Fine-tuning a forecasting network at each point of a parameter grid yields a model zoo indexed by a physical parameter, against which weight-space diagnostics can be checked. We build such model zoos for four dynamical systems and analyse them with JEPAWG, a recently proposed joint-embedding hypernetwork built around a learned parameter--weight representation. It was first introduced for neural samplers for lattice field theories, where its latent geometry located the phase transition and estimated the 2D Ising critical exponent. Applied to dynamical systems, JEPAWG is competitive on forecasting with a hypernetwork trained directly for that task, despite being supervised on the parameter--weight correspondence rather than on forecasts. Beyond forecasting, the norm of the parameter-derivative of the decoded weights locates Hopf points and curves, tracks a period-doubling cascade closely enough to give a qualitative estimate of the Feigenbaum constant, and detects a global bifurcation, which has no eigenvalue signature and is therefore invisible to linearisation. As such, JEPAWG provides interpretable insight into the dynamics that is not available from other hypernetworks. Together, these results indicate that JEPAWG is a workable instrument for reading physical structure off a population of trained networks.

title: Primal-Dual Representation Learning for Low-Rank Constrained MDPs
abstract: Representation learning has substantially improved the efficiency of unconstrained continuous-state Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), but its extension to Constrained MDPs (CMDPs) is difficult because the transition representation must be learned while constraint violation is controlled. In this paper, we study representation learning for low-rank CMDPs with continuous state spaces, and propose REP-PD-TEG for the soft cumulative-violation setting. In the feature learning period, the algorithm interacts with the environment using a decaying-$ε$-greedy mixture execution policy, and uses the collected samples to learn transition features by maximum likelihood. Based on the learned features, it constructs uncertainty bonuses and plans with an optimistic Lagrangian objective to obtain the return policy. We prove regret and soft-violation guarantees for the return policies, and quantify the influence of the decaying-$ε$-greedy exploration. In particular, REP-PD-TEG achieves the optimal $\widetilde O(\sqrt K)$ return policy bound, and gives a $\widetilde O(K^{3/4})$ overall sample bound when exploratory actions are charged. For the stricter hard cumulative violation, where feasibility must be verified episode by episode, we propose REP-PD-H-TEG. It plans under a bonus-corrected lower-confidence utility certificate with the learned representation, and performs a stabilized dual search to obtain the return policy, yielding regret and hard-violation bounds. Together, these results give the first theoretically guaranteed representation-learning method for low-rank continuous-state CMDPs with both soft cumulative guarantees and certified hard-violation control.

title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling
abstract: Text embedding and text generation are two of the most useful capabilities of modern large language models, yet they are typically provided by separate specialized models (an embedder and a generator) trained with incompatible objectives and deployed side by side in retrieval-augmented generation and agent systems. Recent unified embedding-generation models such as GritLM share parameters between the two capabilities, but they either switch attention regimes between modes or optimize embedding and language modeling as parallel objectives that never supervise each other. We argue that these designs are only partially unified: the two capabilities coexist on the same weights, but do not shape each other. We propose ULME, a post-training framework that unifies embedding and language modeling on a causal decoder-only LLM through predictive coupling. ULME inserts a chain of learnable slots between the query and the answer, reads a semantic embedding and a reasoning embedding from two designated slots, and trains three objectives on a shared causal backbone: a contrastive loss anchoring the semantic slot to document representations, a language-modeling loss supervising answer generation, and a stop-gradient predictive loss that aligns the reasoning slot with a pooled summary of the answer, so that generation actively shapes what the embedding encodes. Across two model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and eight scales spanning 0.5B-8B parameters, a single ULME checkpoint improves MTEB by 3.3-4.1 points over the strongest open-source baseline, tightens BRIGHT and AdvBench-IR simultaneously, and remains on par with a generation-only fine-tune on standard accuracy benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval), demonstrating that genuine unification yields mutually reinforcing rather than merely coexisting capabilities.

title: Learning Domain Trajectories with Flow Matching for Gradual Domain Adaptation
abstract: Large distribution shifts remain a primary obstacle for domain generalization and unsupervised adaptation. Although gradual domain adaptation alleviates this difficulty by introducing ordered intermediate domains, most existing approaches still operate in a discrete, step-wise manner, which can accumulate errors and often relies on unstable Min--Max optimization. We propose \textbf{FlowGDA}, a flow-matching framework that models gradual adaptation as \emph{continuous} transport on a statistical manifold in a representation space. FlowGDA learns time-dependent velocity fields that induce smooth domain trajectories, using a simulation-free regression objective rather than adversarial training. To prevent semantic drift, we couple left-to-right transport between consecutive domains with a source-anchored transport and a semantic consistency loss, and we further stabilize learning via a two-stage sequential optimization scheme. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, validating flow matching as an effective alternative for domain adaptation.

title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement
abstract: Deep neural networks often struggle to provide reliable confidence estimates, making post-hoc calibration essential for reliable decision-making. Existing post-hoc methods largely rely on score-based transformations, which improve marginal calibration but often fail to capture spatially varying miscalibration in local regions of the learned feature space. To address this gap, we propose Local Adaptive Probability Estimation (LAPE), a post-hoc residual calibration framework. Specifically, LAPE treats the global calibrator output as a stable anchor and refines the individual prediction by leveraging non-parametric local evidence from neighboring calibration samples. As a plug-and-play refinement module, LAPE effectively utilizes the information about feature-space geometry and can reuse the calibration data that are used to construct the global calibrator. Furthermore, we extend LAPE to the setting with multi-view inputs through Cascade Feature Augmentation Fusion (CFAF). Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods can improve the calibration quality of various existing baselines and remain efficient and robust across different settings.

title: Visual Grounding First, Multimodal In-context Learning Follows
abstract: LLMs have shown strong in-context learning (ICL) capability, but extending it to Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) remains challenging. Prior multimodal ICL methods often rely on ICL-specific datasets for additional training or task vector extraction, which can improve performance on the same ICL benchmark used for adaptation. However, they do not generalize well to other benchmarks and often induce forgetting in previously well-solved tasks. For this reason, we identify 'visual grounding' as the key bottleneck in multimodal ICL; MLLMs often fail to attend to task-relevant visual evidence in demonstrations, instead over-relying on textual cues and producing hallucinated outputs. To address this, we propose ProCoRe to enhance visual grounding through contrastive reinforcement learning on multimodal contrastive data for improving multimodal ICL. ProCoRe generates captions for contrastive image pairs, decomposes them into propositions, and optimizes contrastive rewards that encourage alignment with corresponding images while discouraging mismatched ones. Despite never seeing ICL-formatted training examples, ProCoRe improves average multimodal ICL classification accuracy by 5.6% and captioning ROUGE-L by 13.8% over the off-the-shelf Qwen-VL-3-8B model, outperforming ICL-data-dependent state of the arts across benchmarks. Finally, we introduce PICL, a personalized multimodal ICL captioning benchmark that tests whether MLLMs genuinely understand visual demonstrations rather than relying on pre-trained semantic priors.

title: Behind Aggregate Scores: What Systematically Varying Arena-Hard's LLM Judge Reveals
abstract: LLM judges are used to determine which of two answers is better. Trusting these verdicts requires knowing how repeatable they are and how much they depend on the judge's instructions. We show that similar aggregate scores can conceal substantial changes in individual verdicts, both when the same setup is repeated and when the instructions change. Using 500 Arena-Hard v2.0 prompts with two models' answers held fixed, we run GPT-4.1 as the judge under all eight combinations of criteria, output format and task framing, and repeat every setup unchanged at temperature zero on a pinned model version. Rerunning the default setup moves the aggregate score by about one point but changes the win/tie/loss outcome on 21.2% of prompts. Instruction changes introduce further sensitivity: in one setup, which asks for the verdict without reasoning and also drops several other instructions, outcomes change on 28.2 percentage points more prompts than the two setups' unchanged reruns do on average, and the aggregate score falls by 4.09 points. In another, where the criteria prioritise accuracy, outcomes change on 6.7 percentage points more prompts by the same comparison, while the aggregate score barely moves. A stable aggregate score therefore does not establish that individual verdicts are repeatable. This distinction matters when those verdicts are used as preference labels or to assess individual responses. Evaluations that rely on individual verdicts should repeat each setup they use and report both aggregate scores and prompt-level agreement.

title: Externalise the Memory: A Pre-Registered Study of Where an Embodied Agent's Experience Should Live
abstract: Should an embodied agent's experience be baked into its policy weights, or kept external and retrieved at inference? A memory-augmented teacher (a VLM that retrieves lessons, with their episode images, from its own past attempts) produces trajectories on a vision-conditioned reach task; from the same trajectories we distil LoRA student policies and evaluate them under matched protocols, including one that re-attaches the teacher's frozen retrieval buffer to a fixed set of student weights. We pre-registered the hypotheses, arms, tests, and analysis rules before training and before any p-value. Distilling the memory-augmented behaviour into weights beat an action-only control by +1 pp (n.s.); the registered test proves underpowered for its own minimum effect, so we withdraw - rather than refute - the memory-in-weights claim. Attaching retrieval to a fixed set of student weights added +34 pp (z=5.15), reaching the pooled memory-augmented teacher reference (49.3%); the pre-registered protocol contrast agrees (+23 pp, z=3.36); under a pre-registered auto-reset sensitivity count the two are +36 and +29 pp. An exploratory behavioural probe with pre-registered per-arm predictions is consistent with behavioural distillation transferring the marginal correction but not the conditional, situation-specific correction that retrieval supplies. The recipe that follows is to externalise the memory: in follow-up controls registered before they ran, the same frozen buffer lifts the base model with no adapter to 48% (sensitivity 48%) and the other three adapters from 19-26% to 53-55% (sensitivity 17-21% to 50-55%), and the adapter adds nothing detectable once the buffer is attached. On a second, harder task, the retrieval advantage points the same direction but falls short of significance (+6 pp, 95% CI [-4.5, +16.4]); exploratory diagnostics tie the attenuation to memory coverage.

title: Rethinking SAE Evaluation: An Atomic Interpretable Unit Framework Reveals Hidden Polysemanticity and Redundancy
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) were originally motivated by discovering monosemantic features, a property that characterizes individual features but does not specify what the learned feature set should look like as a whole. As SAEs have increasingly been adopted for attribution, circuit discovery, and intervention, researchers have begun evaluating metrics that describe global properties of the feature set, such as sparsity, dead feature rates, reconstruction fidelity, and disentanglement, a diverse set that extends far beyond monosemanticity. However, this implicit shift beyond monosemanticity has not been formalized as a clear, well-defined objective that comes before these evaluation metrics. Without such an objective, existing metrics remain ad hoc, with their necessity unjustified. In this work, we formalize this ultimate objective by introducing a new paradigm for SAE evaluation: requiring that SAE features, and more generally dictionary-based decompositions of model representations, form an atomic interpretable unit basis, a coordinate system for semantically meaningful explanation. Under this paradigm, we organize existing and new measurements such as DAME (Dominance-Aware Monosemanticity Evaluation) as proxy metrics and introduce a comprehensive benchmarking framework. Evaluating hundreds of SAEs across multiple architectures and model families, we uncover failure modes in which some SAEs appear monosemantic under existing evaluation metrics while remaining functionally polysemantic: the most dominant features, those contributing most to model computation, are systematically less interpretable and more redundant. These failure modes warrant attention from SAE researchers as targets for improved training and architectures, and motivate dominance-aware evaluation as a standard check for practitioners before SAE features are deployed for attribution, circuit tracing, or intervention.

title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
abstract: Reproducing a published 3DGS paper takes weeks of expert engineering before any extension can be proposed. Prior autonomous-research systems read papers, draft hypotheses, and write code, but are limited by short fixed templates, low executability, and weak traceability, and none has been demonstrated end-to-end in a live computer-vision subfield with intense activity. SplatLab is an autonomous research system for 3D Gaussian Splatting that addresses these limitations. Given a research prompt, a target-paper URL, or no input at all, it reproduces a published baseline, proposes an extension, trains and ablates across Mip-NeRF 360 and LLFF, writes the manuscript, and binds every reported number to a logged training run. Five design choices distinguish it: (i) candidates mutate plugins from a verified-reproduction backbone matched to published baselines; (ii) a cascade-weighted Elo tournament across eight islands scores candidates on measured GPU PSNR with verbal-gradient feedback; (iii) a standing falsifier subtracts Elo on failure, integrating stress-test survival into selection; (iv) every reported number is bound to a logged training run, and the run cannot terminate while any claim is unbacked; (v) a seven-category 3DGS taxonomy wraps EVOLVE-BLOCK markers in domain-aligned scaffolds transferable across 3DGS repositories. On PSNR-targeted runs, SplatLab's manuscripts beat their reproduced targets by +0.18 to +3.78 dB, including +3.78 dB on astrophotographic nebula rendering, for which no prior 3DGS method exists. The research cycle compresses from months of graduate-student time to days of mostly autonomous compute. Code, all manuscripts, experiment ledgers, and the cross-run paper store are available on the project page.

title: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
abstract: LLM agents are flexible in language interaction, but using them as long-horizon planners is costly and prone to hallucinated or invalid actions. This paper targets a different role for LLMs: constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning. We propose MemPlan, a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework for partially observable interactive text environments. MemPlan keeps the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructs the PDDL problem at each step from parsed observations, candidate hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive graph memory assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses for missing objects, locations, or conditions, guiding the planner toward more plausible checks. Negative memory records execution-refuted assumptions and compiles them into exclusion constraints, preventing repeated attempts at candidates already contradicted by feedback. A unified schema-conditioned language--symbol interface, trained offline with supervised fine-tuning, connects text environments to the planning loop through observation-to-fact parsing and symbolic-action-to-command grounding. Experiments on TextWorld, ALFWorld, and Robotouille show that MemPlan improves task completion and step efficiency over language-only and PDDL-aware baselines, while substantially reducing online token cost compared with LLM-planning baselines such as ReAct. The same fine-tuned interface is also reused across TextWorld task types without task-specific fine-tuning. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/tewiSong/MemPlan.

title: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz
abstract: Muon updates matrix-valued parameters along approximately orthogonalized directions and often trains large language models faster than AdamW, yet it remains unclear when and why orthogonalization helps. We study PolarGD, the orthogonalized update at the core of Muon, on matrix quadratics, where optimizers can be analyzed in closed form, and compare update directions under line search to remove the effect of learning-rate tuning. Orthogonalization pays off when the gradient is far from low rank and its largest singular directions see high curvature. PolarGD reaches the minimizer in one step whenever the rows of the error are orthogonal with equal norms, for any Hessian, whereas gradient descent needs all Hessian eigenvalues to be equal; and unlike sign descent, PolarGD is unaffected by rotations of the problem. Over many steps, PolarGD acts as gradient descent preconditioned by the current iterate, so its speed is governed by the conditioning of the iterate rather than of the Hessian. This explains fast regimes as well as a slow one, caused by tiny singular values of the iterate, in which PolarGD is much slower than gradient descent. Finally, the few Newton-Schulz iterations used in Muon treat these tiny singular values as gradient descent does, so fewer iterations can converge faster than exact orthogonalization; in a transformer trained with Muon, about a quarter of the singular values of the attention matrices fall in this regime.

title: Velocity Ambiguity Profiles: Time-Resolved Bayes-Risk Diagnostics for Flow Matching
abstract: Flow matching trains a continuum of velocity regression problems but usually reports a loss averaged over interpolation time, obscuring which regions are limited by intrinsic ambiguity and which remain data-limited. We introduce the Velocity Ambiguity Profile (VAP), $\mathcal{A}_v(t)$, the time-local Bayes-risk floor of velocity prediction, and decompose time-resolved loss as $L_N(t)=\mathcal{A}_v(t)+R(t;N)$, where only the excess term $R(t;N)$ is reducible by more data or a different estimator. For $N$ training samples and a $K$-component mixture in the structured example, we prove two statistical benchmarks. In an intrinsic local-regression benchmark, $\mathcal{A}_v(t)$ enters the time-dependent noise factor of the standard nonparametric rate. In separated isotropic Gaussian mixtures, the Bayes velocity becomes locally affine, and a label-oracle residual-regression benchmark has parametric excess-risk scale $K\mathcal{A}_v(t)/N$, matched within the same separated residual Gaussian-location subproblem. Controlled Gaussian-mixture experiments validate this diagnostic through a dense transition sweep, calibrated oracle-to-blind and empirical-proxy audits, and a local controlled time-sampler stress test in which a frozen reducible-error proxy reduces reducible loss while cross-cell sensitivity delimits aggressive sampling. On CIFAR-100 DINOv2 feature flow, guided time sampling reduces uniformly evaluated velocity loss by $6.78\%$ and global feature Fréchet distance (FD) by $23.6\%$, while class-conditional kernel inception distance (KID) shows no improvement. VAP turns an averaged flow-matching objective into a time-resolved diagnostic for locating ambiguity-limited and data-limited regions.

title: SWE-DIVE: Multi-Turn Coding Agent Evaluation with Dynamic User Simulation
abstract: Coding agents are typically evaluated using one-shot, well-formulated prompts. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench use existing GitHub issues as input for a coding agent and evaluate whether the agent successfully solves the task. However, in real-world use cases, prompts are often not as well-formulated or structured as existing GitHub issues. Additionally, a coding agent session is not limited to a single prompt; it typically involves a multi-turn interaction in which the user iteratively adds new tasks and requirements that the agent must fulfill. To benchmark these abilities, we developed SWE-DIVE, a dynamic, interactive validation and evaluation framework for benchmarking coding agents in a multi-turn environment. To achieve this, we introduce a user simulator that can simulate different behavioral patterns and communicate with the coding agent. We also introduce a conversation validator that evaluates the user simulator's outputs to determine whether they fulfill the initial requirements and guide the agent toward successfully solving the task. The entire framework is embedded in a Harbor environment, which orchestrates the coding agent, user simulator, and conversation validator, and executes the test environment to determine whether the agent successfully solves the task. Our results and source code are available in our GitHub repository (https://github.com/lorenzbrehme/swe-dive_usersim).

title: Mitigating Model Collapse through Dreaming Learning
abstract: Training generative models on synthetic data causes loss of diversity and a decrease in performance, a phenomenon known as model collapse. We study this degeneration spectrally in a controlled Markov setting. The eigenvalue spectrum of the learned transition operator offers a direct view of the process, since the subdominant eigenvalues set how fast the chain mixes and therefore how much of the state space it continues to explore. We find that sampling at temperature $T_s 1$. Because high-temperature samples flatten the predicted distribution, training on them keeps the entries of the learned operator from becoming vanishingly small, which in turn keeps the eigenvalues bounded away from the unit circle. Measurements of the spectra over 5000 generations are consistent with this picture, and the mitigation effect persists in more complex settings such as LSTM language models and a 124M-parameter GPT-2.

title: SCDM: Scalable Causal Discovery in Nonlinear Temporal Systems with Meta-Learning
abstract: Causal discovery from nonlinear multivariate time series is challenging in high-dimensional systems, where the number of candidate directed relations grows quadratically with the number of variables. Existing methods are often limited by target-wise model fitting, repeated conditional testing, or expensive graph-search procedures. We propose SCDM, a shared-parameter meta-learning framework for scalable temporal causal discovery. SCDM treats each target variable as a task while learning a shared temporal predictor and a shared causal-strength matrix across tasks. Each meta-episode updates only a subset of target-variable tasks, allowing the model to accumulate structural evidence across the full system without exhaustive target-wise optimization. After training, a post-training graph readout converts the learned predictor into continuous directed causal scores for threshold-independent evaluation. We also provide a finite-error recovery principle showing that, under fully observed delayed-system assumptions and a positive risk-gap condition, thresholding SCDM scores recovers the graph when statistical, meta-optimization, and readout errors are below the population margin. Experiments on controlled synthetic, neuroimaging-inspired, high-dimensional, and real-world temporal benchmarks demonstrate competitive causal recovery and improved scalability in large temporal systems.

title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
abstract: A benchmark is not merely a collection of test questions; it naturally induces an empirical measure over difficulty. In this work, we develop this measure-based view of benchmark evaluation. This perspective allows us to identify and formalize two central failure modes: measure mismatch, where the benchmark difficulty distribution differs from the intended difficulty distribution, and coverage gaps, where uncovered regions along the difficulty axis prevent benchmarks from detecting meaningful localized training progress. We propose two diagnostic metrics that capture these two failure modes and provide rigorous theoretical guarantees. Empirically, we analyze 25 popular benchmarks spanning 7 domains using carefully estimated item difficulties. Our results show that many benchmarks implicitly overweight certain difficulty regions, so their leaderboard conclusions should be interpreted with caution; others leave substantial portions of the difficulty axis uncovered, limiting their ability to monitor the model improvement process. Finally, we turn diagnosis into action by introducing BenchFill, a simple difficulty-targeted item rewriting algorithm that effectively reduces local coverage gaps.

title: Privacy in Context Is Being Overlooked in the Age of General-Purpose LLMs
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) continue to grow in scope and capability, privacy concerns are on the rise. Since users increasingly interact with a single general-purpose system across many distinct contexts, there is a natural tendency to pursue a one-size-fits-all solution to privacy. Unfortunately, this overlooks a crucial insight from decades of privacy research: privacy is inherently contextual. In this paper, we argue that existing work in prompt privacy is drifting towards attempts to design a unified framework, which is highly misleading and can foster a false sense of security. Furthermore, we argue that even future work in this direction needs to wrestle with fundamental tensions across various desirable properties of prompt privacy. Thus, such continued attempts towards a unified framework need to be reconsidered. We recommend three critical paths forward: application-specific deployment of LLMs, context-specific evaluation of privacy frameworks, and better privacy literacy.

title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
abstract: Literature-searching language agents are becoming a standard component of scientific assistants for the life sciences, yet there is little controlled evidence on which parts of their harness matter. We run a controlled ablation on biomedical claim verification (SciFact) with the live PubMed API as the only tool. Holding the backbone and output format fixed, we compare four harnesses: closed-book answering, single-shot retrieval using the claim as the query, a ReAct-style agent that writes its own PubMed queries, and an oracle given the gold abstracts, each with two efficient frontier backbones. Naive single-shot retrieval finds the gold paper for only 6% of claims and turns overconfident errors into abstentions without improving accuracy. Letting the model formulate its own queries triples gold recall and yields the best verdicts (62% accuracy vs. 49-59% for the other realistic harnesses), although these differences are not significant at our sample size and agents use fewer than half of their search budget. With gold abstracts, the same models reach 79-86% accuracy, a significant 17-24 point gap showing that retrieval, not reasoning, is the main bottleneck. Finally, a citation audit shows that closed-book models cite PubMed IDs that almost always exist (327/335) but are almost never relevant: a cross-family LLM judge rates only 3 of 327 existing citations as relevant to the claim, versus 67% for citations produced by the search agent. Existence checks are therefore insufficient safeguards for scientific agents. We release code, prompts, and all cached tool calls at https://github.com/saqlain2204/real-pmids-wrong-papers.

title: MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models scale model capacity efficiently by activating a small subset of parameters per token. However, in long-context inference, memory remains a major bottleneck because the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length. Existing KV cache compression methods reduce this cost for dense transformers, but overlook a problem specific to MoE: KV eviction can change which experts are selected during answer generation, degrading the generation quality. We propose MoEZip, a routing-aware KV cache compression for sparse MoE language models. To estimate the sensitivity of expert routing to perturbation, we propose a novel metric based on the Fisher information matrix of routing distributions. MoEZip combines this metric with attention weights for routing-aware scoring of contexts. Finally, we compose a complementary scoring system that combines eviction methods for dense and sparse-MoE architectures. Experiments show that MoEZip achieves robust performance under aggressive cache compression on various benchmarks. At a KV retention ratio of 10\%, MoEZip improves over the SoTA baseline by +24 and +20 points on average on LongBench and RULER, corresponding to 2.3$\times$ and 4.9$\times$ higher scores, respectively.

title: The Reflexivity Threshold: A Phase Transition for Multi-Agent Performative Prediction
abstract: Many learning systems are performative: once deployed, their predictions change the data distribution on which future models are trained. In multi-agent settings, this feedback is routed through a network of interacting learners, so stability depends not only on the strength of performativity but also on who affects whom. We study repeated retraining in multi-agent performative prediction and identify a spectral threshold that separates stable learning from worst-case learning obstruction.
